display.purpose: Hero headlines and page-level identifiers. One per page maximum.

headline.purpose: Major section titles and organization names.

title.purpose: Card titles, subsection headings, secondary hierarchy.

body.purpose: Default reading copy, description text, body content. Max 75ch line length.

label.purpose: Eyebrow labels, tags, buttons, form field labels. Always visible.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Ambient shadow on card elements at rest. Establishes light elevation without drama.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Increased shadow on hover. Subtle state change; not a dramatic lift.

shadows.name: gold-glow
shadows.purpose: Subtle glow around primary gold accents on hover/focus. Rarely used; reserved for high-emphasis interactions.

shadows.name: green-glow
shadows.purpose: Glow for success/validated states. Uses tighter chroma to avoid obnoxiousness.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (button hover, focus ring appearance).

motion.name: duration-200
motion.purpose: Quick micro-interactions (button hover, shadow shift, color transitions).

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: Tablet (iPad). Navigation collapses to hamburger menu here.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: Wide desktop. Optional, for ultra-wide displays.

narrative.overview:
Daanaa is built on a commitment to specificity over vibes. Every design choice serves the mission: help donors make more informed and sincere giving decisions.

The visual system reflects this through precise, evidence-based copy; a warm but authoritative palette (navy + cream + gold); and semantic, never-decorative component patterns.

The typography pairing of Cormorant Garamond (editorial serif for headings) and DM Sans (humanistic sans for body) signals care and intention without pretense. The navy establishes trust and professionalism; the cream adds warmth and approachability; the gold provides intentional accent without noise.
keyCharacteristics: Specificity over marketing vagueness — every copy line must be provable from data or user behavior
Respectful of all organizations — small community orgs treated with the same dignity as national foundations
Evidence-based trust signals — no shame language; no unverified claims
Transparent about limitations — acknowledge gaps in data, methodology, and what users should verify directly
Accessible and semantic — WCAG AA compliance is non-negotiable

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Soft Gold is used on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point — it should feel intentional, not defaulted.

rules.name: The No Shame Rule
rules.body: Tier colors intentionally progress from bright to pale, never from 'good' (green) to 'bad' (red). The palette resists judgment language; every org is presented with equal dignity.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-For-Headings Rule
rules.body: Cormorant Garamond is used only for h1–h4 and major section headings. Never in body text or UI labels. The readability tax is too high.

rules.name: The Line-Length Rule
rules.body: Body text paragraphs must not exceed 75ch. Narrow columns improve scannability and reading comfort.

rules.name: The Mobile-First Rule
rules.body: Design for 375px first, then expand thoughtfully. Never just 'stack desktop columns vertically' — rethink layout, typography sizing, touch targets, and hierarchy for mobile.

rules.name: The Proximity Rule
rules.body: Related items sit closer (8–16px). Distinct sections sit farther (32–48px). Use this spacing as a visual grammar of relationship.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear only as a response to interaction (hover, focus, elevation) or to establish container hierarchy (cards on white background).

dos: Use semantic token names (text-soft-gold, bg-success-green) instead of raw Tailwind utilities
Use component abstractions (Button, Card, Heading, Input) for all UI elements
Test all interactive elements for ≥44×44px touch target and WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text/UI)
Use Cormorant Garamond only for headings (h1–h5); never in body text
Write specific, evidence-based copy ('Browse 1.7M nonprofits indexed from IRS records' vs. 'Discover causes you care about')
Acknowledge data gaps and limitations ('This data is 12–24 months old per IRS filing timelines')
Respect all organization sizes equally — no size-based ranking or shame language
Use proper icons (Lucide, Heroicons) instead of emoji in functional UI
Keep gold accent use to ≤10% of any screen
donts: Use raw Tailwind color utilities (bg-green-600, text-red-700). Use semantic tokens instead
Build custom button/card/heading styles. Use the component abstraction
Use emoji as UI iconography (❌ '🎯 Financial Health'). Use icon fonts or SVG
Center all headings, descriptions, and buttons. Left-align for scannability; center only hero sections
Add decorative elements (wavy dividers, floating blobs, ornamental shadows) unless content is insufficient
Use shade.scss or custom color values. All colors come from index.css CSS variables or tailwind.config.js
Create new heading levels or font sizes outside the defined type scale
Hardcode hex colors in component style attributes. Always use semantic tokens or Tailwind class names
Ship unverified or experimental outputs as established fact. Mark uncertain guidance as 'provisional'
Use shame language or negative framing ('Poor financial health', 'Bottom-tier org'). Use neutral descriptors
